opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the role owns the Payroll system, the maximum access level is admin. Requested write access is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E031 as a contractor with basic security training (note: HR listed full-time). As a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed access is read. Requested write exceeds this maximum, so recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting employee information for E031: HR lists the employee as full-time Payroll Specialist (recommending write), while the Security DB lists the employee as a contractor with basic security training (recommending read), and Security explicitly flagged this discrepancy. Under the contractor classification, the maximum allowed access to Payroll is read (basic training, no admin), so the requested write exceeds the maximum and must be capped at read. Read is also within policy under either classification, making it the conservative, policy-compliant decision.
